title: Fixed-scalar candidate compositor on an etale input
statement: Let A be a finite commutative ring in Type (u+1), and let f:X→Y and g:Y→Z be quasi-compact morphisms between Noetherian schemes, supplied with compactifications cf,cg,cfg. Conjugate the canonical full-etale-origin compositor [thm-sf-comp-composition] to these candidates by towerCandidateComparison [def-sf-origin-candidate-comparison], using the inverse comparison at cfg. The resulting natural isomorphism finiteSupportCandidateComposition, evaluated at the comparison inverse image of any bounded-below etale complex L on X, is exactly coherenceProEtaleCompositor A cf cg cfg L from [lem-pur-compact-support-site-coherence]. There is no operation datum or coefficient-presentation equivalence in this assertion.

source.place: Composition/coherence sentence; the compactification-boundary calculation in step 2 of lem-sf-finite-support-origin-binary-normalization.

proof.text: Prove the four-factor construction and its component formula first for abstract categories and functors, so concrete derived functors stay outside the naturality calculation. Apply this construction to obtain the candidate compositor componentwise from the first candidate comparison mapped by the second support functor, the second candidate comparison, the canonical origin compositor, and the inverse final candidate comparison. Naturality of these four factors proves naturality of the construction. Precompose a candidate comparison with the etale-origin equivalence: its fully faithful preimage construction evaluates to site comparison, etale compactification change, and inverse site comparison. The compact-support site-coherence refinement square identifies this with coherenceCompactificationChange. The reverse site square and the etale comparison inverse law identify its inverse on etale inputs with the reverse comparison.

At an etale input L, the first chosen support is identified with etale support of L by the compact-support site comparison. Naturality of the second candidate comparison conjugates it by that identification. The chosen origin compositor evaluates to originCompositionModel by its preimage construction. Substituting the three compactification-change comparisons produces precisely the six factors defining coherenceCompositionData.proMap and hence coherenceProEtaleCompositor. All steps are natural isomorphism cancellation and also hold for zero and identity inputs.

proof_origin.place: The compactification-boundary part of the binary finite support normalization argument.

lean.statement:
theorem finiteSupportCandidateComposition_etale (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [Finite A]
    {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] [IsNoetherian Y] [IsNoetherian Z]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiCompact g]
    (cf : Compactification f) (cg : Compactification g)
    (cfg : Compactification (f ≫ g))
    (L : DerivedCategory.Plus (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A))) :
    letI := cf.hasCompactification
    letI := cg.hasCompactification
    letI := cfg.hasCompactification
    (finiteSupportCandidateComposition A f g cf cg cfg).hom.app
        ((comparisonUpperStarPlusEtaleOrigin (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) X).obj L) =
      coherenceProEtaleCompositor A cf cg cfg L
